t: Section 955 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 1896; 10 U.S.C. 129a note) is repealed.

fable.w: This section simply repeals a provision of a prior National Defense Authorization Act. It establishes no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation language at all; a bare repeal is not a participatory process.

qwen_block.w: This section simply repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any new process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It is a legislative housekeeping provision that removes existing law rather than creating a mechanism for public or external input.
qwen_block.s: Section 955 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 1896; 10 U.S.C. 129a note) is repealed.

opus.w: The section only repeals an earlier statutory provision. It does not ask the government to consult outside parties, hold a hearing, take comments, issue rules or set up an advisory body. Reading participation into it would mean going beyond the text, which involves no one outside the federal government in any decision.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The only possible trap is reading something into the repealed provision. Section 955 of the FY2013 NDAA dealt with planning for the Defense Department's civilian and contractor workforce. This section simply repeals it. The text itself sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. Nobody outside the federal government is involved in any decision.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section merely repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any new requirement for the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties, nor does it describe a process involving non-federal actors. Repealing a law is a legislative action that does not inherently constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Section 955 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 1896; 10 U.S.C. 129a note) is repealed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that repealing a section could implicitly remove a participation requirement, or that the repealed section itself contained participation. However, the text provided is merely a repeal clause. It does not establish, require, or describe any process of consultation, coordination, or involvement with outside parties. It simply removes existing law. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
